featured.thesis: When the Sep 9–10 coupon reopenings clear strong at multi-decade-high yields and the first enlarged long-end buyback still leaves 10s through ~5% and 30s near 5.3%, the regime is not "failed auctions" — it is the price of sponsorship: private cover exists only at yields that behave like a credit spread, and the state bid is insurance that does not buy the long end. Money is in who warehouses duration at these clearing yields — not Nvidia, not AGI timeline theater.
featured.who_collects_rent: Captive duration absorbers (banks/pensions via HTM/SLR/rules); primary dealers as thin warehouse; Treasury buyback ops as liquidity insurance — franchise ROE / accounting on forced holdings at higher equilibrium yields; dealer fees; state bid as cosmetic backstop. Leftover: soft-landing / Fed-cut coupon narrative.
featured.decisive_test: (1) Nov 4 QRA — buyback maxes cut or framed temporary → RELEGATE. (2) Sustained FRED CMT 10y back below ~4.50% with buyback ops idle/undersubscribed → price-of-sponsorship thesis weakens. (3) Next long coupon (20y when announced; Oct 6–7 3y/10y) — soft cover/fat tail/weak indirects with thick buybacks → sponsorship stress tightens (WATCH, not RELEGATE). (4) FOMC+SEP Sep 15–16 — sticky/higher long yields after front-end move = regime intact; long-end rally repairing 10s30s with quiet buybacks = falsifier to watch.
